bugs.title: Same shift shows different lifecycle status across pages
bugs.page: worker dashboard/detail, employer dashboard/detail/calendar, public list, admin
bugs.steps: Open the same shift on the worker dashboard card and the worker detail page (and the employer's two surfaces) near its start time.
bugs.expected: One canonical lifecycle state; the same label everywhere at the same instant.
bugs.actual: Worker dashboard/card showed 'Sắp bắt đầu', worker detail showed 'Đang diễn ra', employer dashboard 'Đang diễn ra', employer detail 'Sắp bắt đầu' — because the codebase had TWO competing status systems (stored Shift.status via ShiftStatusBadge, and live getShiftDisplayPhase via ShiftPhaseChip) used inconsistently across pages.
bugs.fix: Added src/domain/shiftLifecycleState.ts: getShiftLifecycleState(shift, applications, nowIso) returns ONE canonical state (Draft/PendingDeposit/Published/StartingSoon/InProgress/AwaitingCheckout/AwaitingEmployerConfirmation/Completed/Expired/Cancelled/Disputed). A single ShiftLifecycleBadge component renders it on every surface with the same (shift, applications, now). Removed the page-local ShiftPhaseChip and the raw ShiftStatusBadge usages.

bugs.title: Check-in / employer mark-present appeared to advance the shift lifecycle
bugs.steps: Worker checks in before start, or employer marks present before start.
bugs.expected: Shift lifecycle depends on the wall clock only; presence is an application/attendance fact.
bugs.actual: Because the live phase chip read check-in presence, a check-in before start could make the UI read as if the shift had started.
bugs.fix: getShiftLifecycleState's time rules never read check-in/mark-present for the start/end transitions. A shift is InProgress iff now >= start && now < end, regardless of presence. Presence is read only to distinguish AwaitingCheckout from Expired after end. Verified the lifecycle state is identical with/without a check-in at the same now.
tests: src/__tests__/coreStability10.test.ts (lifecycle identical with/without check-in; mark-present before start stays StartingSoon)

bugs.title: Check-out could appear before shift end
bugs.steps: Self-check-in to a shift and look for the check-out CTA before the shift end time.
bugs.expected: Check-out only after shift end (within the 60-minute grace), only for a self-checked-in worker.
bugs.actual: Re-asserted: checkout must never appear before end (the CS9 gate already enforced now>=end; CS10 adds the cross-role/time-travel coverage and confirms the worker dashboard hides it mid-shift).
bugs.fix: canCheckOut requires now >= end AND status CheckedIn AND own checkInAt. The worker dashboard gates the checkout button on canCheckOut. Employer-marked-present alone never unlocks checkout.
tests: src/__tests__/coreStability10.test.ts (checkout never before end; employer-only never unlocks)

bugs.title: Employer attendance actions incomplete / absent button hidden
bugs.steps: Open an applicant row during the attendance window.
bugs.expected: Both 'Đánh dấu có mặt' and 'Đánh dấu vắng mặt' shown when eligible; if worker checked in, absent stays visible but disabled/dimmed with a reason.
bugs.actual: Re-asserted and tested: present + absent pairing, absent disabled+dimmed with reason for a checked-in worker, absent independent of evidenceRequirement.
bugs.fix: ApplicationActionButtons renders both actions gated by canEmployerMarkPresent / canEmployerMarkAbsent; a checked-in worker shows the disabled+dimmed absent button with 'Người làm đã check-in. Chỉ đánh dấu vắng mặt nếu có tranh chấp.' canEmployerMarkAbsent does not read evidenceRequirement.
tests: src/__tests__/coreStability10.test.ts (present+absent eligibility; checked-in disables absent; None evidence still allows absent)

bugs.title: Role-aware copy still cross-perspective
bugs.steps: Compare the attendance banner an employer sees vs a worker.
bugs.expected: Worker uses 'bạn'; employer uses 'người làm'/'bạn đã xác nhận'; admin neutral. No employer page shows 'Nhà tuyển dụng đã xác nhận bạn…'.
bugs.actual: Audited: the role-aware attendance.copy.{worker|employer|admin}.* keys from CS9 are correct and the legacy cross-perspective lifecycle.mismatch.* keys are no longer referenced by any UI component.
bugs.fix: Confirmed worker dashboard uses attendanceCopyKey(state,'worker') and employer detail uses 'employer'. Verified no UI references lifecycle.mismatch.*. Added per-role key-distinctness tests.

bugs.title: Badge colours inconsistent (InProgress purple vs blue/green)
bugs.steps: Compare the 'Đang diễn ra' badge colour on a card vs on the detail page.
bugs.expected: Same state = same label + same colour everywhere.
bugs.actual: InProgress was purple via ShiftStatusBadge but green/success via the phase chip; labels also differed.
bugs.fix: getShiftStatusBadge(state) is the ONE mapping {labelKey, tone, priority}. InProgress is always 'info' (blue). ShiftLifecycleBadge uses it everywhere. Escrow badge stays visually separate. Calendar tile colour keyed by lifecycle state too.
tests: src/__tests__/coreStability10.test.ts (Part 6 badge mapping; InProgress=info not purple/green)

productDecisions.decision: Shift lifecycle is a pure function of the wall clock for start/end transitions. Check-in and employer mark-present are application/attendance facts and never move the shift lifecycle.
StartingSoon is a distinct state within 15 minutes before start; it is amber and never overlaps InProgress (blue). A shift that has started never reads 'Sắp bắt đầu'.

On the worker's OWN upcoming card, the public recruiting label 'Đang tuyển' (plain Published, far from start) is suppressed in favour of the worker's application-status badge ('Đã duyệt'). The unified lifecycle badge appears from StartingSoon onwards, identical to every other surface. Recruiting is a discovery concern, not the approved worker's.

getShiftDisplayPhase and ShiftStatusBadge are retained (still exported, still covered by prior tests) but are no longer the rendered lifecycle badge on any page; the single source of truth is getShiftLifecycleState + ShiftLifecycleBadge.
